title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for quantum sensing, overcoming standard quantum limits.
motivation: Quantum sensing typically suffers from decoherence that limits scaling to the standard quantum limit; achieving Heisenberg scaling in time is crucial for high-precision measurements.
method: The authors propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme using engineered dissipation to protect the sensor qubit, enabling continuous error correction without active measurement or feedback.
result: They show that the scheme can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in time, with the sensing precision scaling as 1/T, where T is the total sensing time, even in the presence of noise.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction provides a practical route to surpass the standard quantum limit in time-continuous quantum sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond two-outcome settings for better detection of nonlocality and entanglement in multipartite systems, and to connect them to practical many-body observables.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements based on spin-nematic operators, and analyzes their violation in spin-squeezed states and other many-body states.
result: The inequalities provide tighter bounds for dimension witnessing and can detect spin-nematic squeezing, offering a new tool for quantum information processing with continuous-variable-like systems.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities are a valuable resource for characterizing nonlocality and squeezing in many-body systems, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum networks.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators fabricated on germanium quantum well heterostructures, a key component for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Ge quantum wells are a promising platform for hole spin qubits, but integrating high-performance microwave resonators is challenging due to material constraints. This work aims to develop resonators that maintain high quality factors under magnetic fields, essential for qubit readout and coupling.
method: The authors design and fabricate superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, characterizing their performance at millikelvin temperatures and under applied magnetic fields using standard microwave reflectometry.
result: The resonators achieve internal quality factors exceeding 10^5 at low power and remain resilient to in-plane magnetic fields up to several Tesla, with minimal degradation.
conclusion: These results establish Ge quantum well heterostructures as a viable platform for high-coherence circuit QED, enabling scalable spin-photon interfaces for quantum information processing.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped-ion qubits are a leading platform for quantum computing, but precise control of complex phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and error correction. This work aims to achieve such control using optical methods.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with optical addressing to manipulate the qubit phase via stimulated Raman transitions, employing a combination of laser pulses and phase modulation techniques.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity phase control with low error rates, showing the ability to implement arbitrary single-qubit phase gates and characterize the coherence properties.
conclusion: Optical control of complex phases in trapped-ion qubits is feasible and can be integrated into larger quantum circuits, advancing the trapped-ion platform for quantum computing.

title: Louvre: Relaxing Hardware Requirements Of Quantum Ldpc Codes By Routing With Expanded Quantum Instruction Set
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a routing-based approach to relax hardware connectivity requirements for quantum LDPC codes using an expanded quantum instruction set.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low overhead but require high connectivity, which is challenging for near-term hardware. This work aims to reduce connectivity demands by introducing routing operations.
method: The authors design an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling the implementation of LDPC codes on hardware with limited connectivity. They analyze the trade-offs between routing overhead and code performance.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the required hardware connectivity for implementing quantum LDPC codes, with manageable overhead in terms of additional gates and time.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a practical approach to make quantum LDPC codes feasible on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum error correction implementation.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entangled strategies can enforce fairness in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomized games often suffer from unfair advantages due to imperfect randomness or cheating. The authors aim to leverage quantum entanglement to guarantee fairness without trusted third parties.
method: They design a quantum game where players share entangled states and perform measurements; the game's outcome is determined by quantum correlations, ensuring that no player can bias the result unilaterally.
result: The entangled protocol achieves provable fairness, outperforming classical randomization in terms of resistance to cheating and efficiency.
conclusion: Entanglement can serve as a practical resource for fairness in multi-party protocols, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and distributed computing.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates high threshold and low logical error rates under circuit-level noise, with runtime scaling almost linearly with code length.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and robust, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;

method: A periodic array of polar vortices in a ferroelectric material is modulated by an electric field via piezoelectric effect, creating a strain wave grating that diffracts X-rays.
result: The piezoelectric grating successfully generates and controls nanoscale strain waves, as evidenced by X-ray diffraction patterns.
conclusion: Polar vortex structures can serve as reconfigurable diffraction gratings for strain waves, offering a new tool for nanoscale wave manipulation.

conclusion: Neural tangent kernels offer a practical framework for diagnosing quantum neural networks, but the work is primarily a machine learning analysis without deep quantum information or thermodynamics insights.
